reasons: Required fields can reject normal results when metadata is missing.

terms.meaning: A library that checks that data has the right shape and types.
A field that is allowed to hold no value.
The written description of what each request and reply must contain.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for data models
sections.what: Loads the data-checking library and the type labels used to describe the fields.
sections.why: Likely reason: needed to define the models below.

sections.name: IndexFolderRequest
sections.title: Index folder request format
sections.what: Describes what the index request contains: the folder path, whether to include subfolders, and the collection name.
sections.why: Likely reason: defines the request contract and defaults the frontend can omit.
sections.watch_out: The folder path is required, while subfolders are included by default.

sections.name: IndexFolderResponse
sections.title: Index folder reply format
sections.what: Describes the indexing reply: a success flag, a message, and a free-form statistics dictionary.
sections.why: Likely reason: the statistics can change shape without changing this model.
sections.watch_out: The routes read a processed file count from the statistics, so if that key is missing the reply fails.

sections.name: QueryRequest
sections.title: Query request format
sections.what: Describes a question request: the question text, how many results to fetch, optional filters, and the collection name.
sections.why: Likely reason: defines the defaults used when the frontend leaves values out.
sections.watch_out: The results count has no upper limit here, so a very large value makes the search slower.

sections.name: Source
sections.title: Source citation format
sections.what: Describes one citation: file name, file path, SharePoint link, page, slide, sheet, and relevance score.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps citations in one consistent shape.
sections.watch_out: The link and location fields have no default, so every source must include them, even when empty.

sections.name: Evidence
sections.title: Evidence item format
sections.what: Describes one search result: its rank, text, score, file details, location, and last modified date.
sections.why: Likely reason: matches the evidence items built by the agent.
sections.watch_out: The chunk index and file type are required, so a search result missing either value fails validation.

sections.name: QueryResponse
sections.title: Query reply format
sections.what: Describes the full answer reply: the query, answer, sources, evidence, analysis, confidence label, and metadata.
sections.why: Likely reason: the frontend depends on these fields being present.
sections.watch_out: The analysis must be a dictionary, so a model reply that parses to a list would fail.

sections.name: ListFoldersRequest
sections.title: List folders request format
sections.what: Describes a request to list SharePoint folders, with a default path of Shared Documents.
sections.why: Likely reason: the default matches the common main document library name.
sections.watch_out: The default name only fits the usual SharePoint library, so other sites must send an explicit path.

sections.name: FolderInfo
sections.title: Folder entry format
sections.what: Describes one SharePoint folder: its name, server path, and created and modified times.
sections.why: Likely reason: matches what the SharePoint client returns.
sections.watch_out: The times are stored as text and are not checked as dates.

sections.name: ListFoldersResponse
sections.title: Folder list reply format
sections.what: Describes the folder list reply: a success flag, the folders, and a total.
sections.why: Likely reason: gives the frontend a consistent list reply.
sections.watch_out: The total is not checked against the list length.

sections.name: FileInfo
sections.title: File entry format
sections.what: Describes one SharePoint file: name, server path, length, created and modified times, and file type.
sections.why: Likely reason: matches what the SharePoint client returns for files.
sections.watch_out: The length is required and must be a whole number, so a file without a length fails.

sections.name: ListFilesRequest
sections.title: List files request format
sections.what: Describes a request to list files in a SharePoint folder, with a default path and an optional recursive flag.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the frontend ask for files in one folder or in all subfolders.
sections.watch_out: The recursive default here is off, while the indexing request defaults to on, which is easy to confuse.

sections.name: ListFilesResponse
sections.title: File list reply format
sections.what: Describes the file list reply: a success flag, the files, and a total.
sections.why: Likely reason: consistent reply shape with the folder list.
sections.watch_out: The total is not checked against the list length.

sections.name: CollectionInfo
sections.title: Collection entry format
sections.what: Describes one saved collection: its name and a free-form statistics dictionary.
sections.why: Likely reason: statistics may vary by store type.
sections.watch_out: The statistics are free-form, so the frontend must handle any keys.

sections.name: ListCollectionsResponse
sections.title: Collection list reply format
sections.what: Describes the collection list reply: a success flag and the list of collections.
sections.watch_out: Collections are read from disk folders, so a stray folder appears in the list.

sections.name: DeleteCollectionRequest
sections.title: Delete collection request format
sections.what: Describes a request to delete a collection by name.
sections.why: Likely reason: the name is required, so nothing is deleted by accident.
sections.watch_out: The name goes straight to a folder deletion, and this model does not check it for path pieces.

sections.name: DeleteCollectionResponse
sections.title: Delete collection reply format
sections.what: Describes the deletion reply: a success flag and a message.
sections.why: Likely reason: confirms the deletion result to the screen.

sections.name: HealthResponse
sections.title: Health reply format
sections.what: Describes the health reply: a status, a version, and a dictionary of service states.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the frontend show each service's state.
sections.watch_out: The version here is typed separately from the version in other files, so it can drift.

summary: Defines the shape of the data sent to and returned by the API, so the backend can check requests and keep replies consistent.
purpose: Makes sure requests have the right fields and types, and gives the API its written description.
why: Likely reason: catching bad data at the edge is simpler than debugging it deeper in the code.
how: Each class lists its fields, their types, and whether they may be empty. The web framework reads these classes to check each request and to shape each reply.
inputs: JSON request bodies from the frontend and results from the agent and SharePoint code.
outputs: Checked request objects and reply objects with the declared fields.
risks: Some fields are required, so a search result missing chunk_index or file_type causes a validation error and a failed reply. Analysis must be a dictionary, not a list.
debug: Validation errors list the field that failed. Check the metadata for the search result or the analysis value that caused it.
